title: Establish sustained token-rate litmus and regression alerting for core model fleet
creator: Marco Chen
description: Build and maintain a repeatable microbenchmark suite that measures sustained tokens-per-second (steady-state throughput) and key tail latency (p95/p99) across our primary model variants. The suite should be KV-cache aware, support variable sequence-length mixes, and produce deterministic fingerprints that enable automatic regression detection and alerting. This ticket covers design, implementation, dashboards, and the first six-week run to capture baseline fingerprints for the core fleet.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible harness that can run against a model variant (hosted/dedicated/private) and emit tokens/sec and p95/p99 metrics
Benchmarks include configurable workload profiles (short/medium/long sequences) and a mixed-length traffic generator
Automatic fingerprint artifact produced per run (hash of config + stable aggregated metrics) stored in S3/GCS
Regression detector that compares latest fingerprint to baseline and flags >10% sustained TPS drop or >20% p95 increase
Dashboard with historical TPS/p95 trends and auto-opened alerts for regressions
Runbook documenting how to create a new baseline, interpret alerts, and kick off forced re-benchmarks
implementation_notes: Harness will reuse existing microbench scaffolding but add: sequence-mix profiles, KV-cache warmup stage, and a steady-state timer to ignore initial ramp artifacts
Use the existing runner image (ci/bench-runner:v2) and extend with a 'sustained' mode that issues long sessions rather than single-shot requests
Metric collection via Prometheus + custom exporter that emits tokens/s, per-request latency histogram, and session-level throughput
Fingerprint composition: model id, quantization profile, runner image tag, seed, workload profile, kv-warmup-duration, aggregated metrics (median TPS, p95, error-rate), then SHA256
Regression detector runs as a scheduled job in infra (k8s CronJob) and posts findings to #bench-alerts and creates ENG tickets for failures
testing_plan: Unit tests for workload generator (sequence mix correctness) and fingerprint hashing
Integration tests in staging that run 10-minute sustained profiles against a test model and validate metrics emitted
Canary run against a non-production model in production cluster to validate no interference with serving capacity
End-to-end smoke run that verifies dashboard ingestion and alert rule firing (simulated regression)
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (this ticket): implement harness, run against 3 core models (small/medium/large) to collect baseline fingerprints
Phase 2: wire regression detector + dashboard, run daily for 2 weeks and tune alert thresholds to reduce false positives
Phase 3: integrate with CI gating for model onboarding PRs and add per-release baseline capture step
Communicate to platform teams and add docs/guide in Confluence with examples and troubleshooting steps
risks: Long sustained runs could impact shared capacity if not isolated; we'll schedule low-traffic windows and prefer dedicated pods
False positives from metric variance — requires statistical smoothing and a short history window to avoid noise-triggered tickets
KV-cache warmup sensitivity across model flavors might require model-specific warmup durations
Storage costs for long-term artifacts if retention not limited
